articles.title: Shakira and Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters once planned to transform a 650-acre Bahamas island with boutique hotels, luxury residences and an artists’ retreat; it is now listed for $30 million
articles.summary: A private island in the northern Bahamas was once at the centre of an ambitious property venture involving Colombian singer Shakira and Pink Floyd
articles.body: A private island in the northern Bahamas was once at the centre of an ambitious property venture involving Colombian singer Shakira and Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters. The plan was to create a destination where artists could stay and work, alongside boutique hotels and luxury residences. The project never progressed as intended, leaving Bonds Cay with a different story from the one its investors had envisaged. According to Mansion Global reports, this 650-acre island is being offered for $30 million, bringing renewed attention to a property that has remained largely undeveloped despite its association with two internationally recognised musicians. Its existing facilities include beachside bungalows and a bar, while the surrounding waters are known for sport fishing.How Shakira and Roger Waters became linked to Bonds CayBonds Cay, part of the Berry Islands in the northern Bahamas, was previously owned by a group of investors that included Shakira and Waters. The island was listed for $16 million in 2006, according to Mansion Global, which reported that the group intended to develop it into an artists' retreat supported by hotels and residential properties. This brought together a private-island purchase and a larger commercial vision, with accommodation and cultural activities forming parts of the same development.The island's association with the musicians dates back to a period when the property was being considered for substantial redevelopment. Their involvement placed Bonds Cay among the unusual property ventures connected with figures from the entertainment industry. However, the purchase did not lead to the planned destination, and the available reporting does not establish precisely when the investors' involvement ended or who owns the island today.A master plan blending luxury stays with the artsThe proposed development went beyond building holiday accommodation across a tropical island. Rafael Viñoly Architects was commissioned to prepare a master plan for Bonds Cay, which stretches approximately 4.25 miles in length, as reported by Rafael Viñoly Architects. The architectural practice described a proposed resort community designed to operate throughout the year, with arts and cultural programming forming a central part of the scheme.The idea was to combine hospitality and residential development with space for creative work. Hotels and luxury apartments would have given visitors somewhere to stay, while the arts programme was intended to distinguish the project from a conventional island resort. The plans offered a way to develop the property commercially while giving it a defined cultural identity.What the $30 million asking price coversThe island is now being marketed for $30 million, according to Mansion Global, which reported the proposed sale in January 2026. The asking price is almost twice the $16 million figure at which Bonds Cay was listed in 2006, although the two amounts refer to different market periods and do not establish a verified change in the property's value.Note: The current owner's identity, the date of the most recent transfer or the price paid in any subsequent transaction is not being specified.Listing agent Gavin Christie of Corcoran C.A. Christie Bahamas presented the property as a large private holding with extensive beaches and shallow turquoise waters. At 650 acres, Bonds Cay offers substantial space for a future owner to consider a range of uses, subject to the relevant development requirements. Its size is central to the current marketing, particularly for buyers considering a resort or a private residential project.Christie identified several possible directions for the island, including a luxury resort, a residential enclave or a secluded family retreat. These are potential uses rather than confirmed developments. There is no indication that a new owner has committed to reviving the original artists' retreat proposal.Bungalows and a beachfront bar remain on the islandAlthough the larger development failed to materialise, Bonds Cay is not without existing facilities. The property has bungalows arranged for glamping, a form of accommodation that combines outdoor surroundings with more comfortable overnight stays. A beachfront bar is also in place, providing a facility for guests and gatherings.Access is possible by boat, seaplane or helicopter, according to the listing details. The island's relative isolation is part of its appeal, but it is not entirely removed from major travel centres. Christie said Bonds Cay is about 37 miles from Nassau, the Bahamian capital, and 155 miles from Fort Lauderdale in Florida.Those distances provide context for the island's potential as a holiday destination. A buyer could explore retaining the existing accommodation or pursuing a more extensive redevelopment, depending on the intended use.The surrounding waters and wildlife add to its appealBonds Cay sits within the Berry Islands, a group of islands and cays in the northern Bahamas. The surrounding waters are popular with sport-fishing enthusiasts and support several sought-after species, including blue marlin, white marlin, sailfish, wahoo and tuna. That marine environment is one of the property's established attractions, separate from any future construction plans.The island also has a distinctive natural feature on land. According to the Mansion Global report, Bonds Cay is the exclusive habitat of a land-snail species discovered there in 1921. Its presence adds another consideration for any prospective development, particularly if plans were to involve substantial changes to the island's natural landscape.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available reports. The Times of India has not independently verified the information presented. The $30 million figure is the reported asking price, not a confirmed sale value.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Uni of Herts handyman sacked for creating mustard gas
articles.summary: Anthony Brown was testing and topping up pool chemicals when he created mustard gas by accident.
articles.body:
A handyman was fairly dismissed after he "inadvertently" created mustard gas that led to a university pool and gym being evacuated, a tribunal found.

Anthony Brown, who worked for Pinnacle FM, had been topping up chemicals and testing pool water at the University of Hertfordshire when the incident occurred on 12 October 2024.

Brown, who had been employed by the firm for seven years and had a "long, unblemished service", was dismissed in November 2024 following an internal investigation.

An employment judge at the Watford tribunal found he "wilfully breached health and safety rules" and the incident could have been avoided.

The tribunal had been told during the maintenance of the pool, Brown had "wedged open" a chlorine tap with a piece of wood before answering a phone call and stepping outside.

On returning, he discovered the tank had overflowed.

He continued his duties before finding another spillage in a different room, this time containing sodium bisulphate.

Brown attempted to clean up both spillages using a vacuum cleaner designed for liquids, draining and flushing it with water.

But during this process, he started a chemical reaction, with an employment tribunal hearing he "inadvertently made mustard gas".

After feeling side affects, Brown notified his manager, resulting in the fire service being called and the pool and gym being evacuated, while Brown was checked by paramedics.

A short time later, it was declared safe and was reopened.

A report by his employer concluded Brown had attempted a "good deed" but had actually "increased the risk of harm to himself and others".

The investigation found that although Brown had a "long, unblemished service", he was guilty of a serious breach of health and safety which could have been avoided, and he was sacked.

The tribunal learned that Brown had not had adequate training in how to deal with spillages, amounting to "essentially one paragraph in a 200-page handbook", with no direct teaching or training ever carried out on chemical leaks.

But it found by propping open the valve and walking away, Brown's actions were the "catalyst" for the chain of events and his conduct amounted to a "deliberate and wilful breach of health and safety rules".

The tribunal dismissed his claims of wrongful and unfair dismissal in a written judgement published on 12 October.

Mustard gas is a man-made blistering agent used in warfare, which causes severe burns to skin, eyes and lungs.

A spokesperson for Pinnacle said: "The safety of our colleagues, clients and customers is our absolute priority.

"We take incidents of this nature extremely seriously and are committed to maintaining the highest standards of health and safety across our operations."

articles.title: ‘Get ready to lose 2029 polls’: Amit Shah warns Rahul Gandhi with Congress poll history
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Tuesday said Congress leader Rahul Gandhi should “introspect” rather than blame the Election Commission (EC)
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Tuesday said Congress leader Rahul Gandhi should “introspect” rather than blame the Election Commission (EC) or the SIR exercise for the opposition party’s electoral setbacks, citing its defeats in the recent byelections and the Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation polls."I also wish to ask Rahul ji: is this the result of an 'SIR'? You dismiss the popularity of the BJP and Modi ji by attributing it to an 'SIR'. You need to introspect," Shah said.Shah also highlighted the Congress's continued poll losses in Gujarat, pointing to its defeat in the Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation polls, held in the state capital.“In a major state (Gujarat) where you (Rahul Gandhi) once held power, you have failed to win a single election in 41 years. This is a matter that demands serious introspection on their (Congress') part,” the senior BJP leader added.The home minister then listed the BJP's victories in the byelections to the Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats in West Bengal and the Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency in Assam, where the party's candidates won by large margins in last week's bypolls.He also mentioned the Thattanchavady assembly seat in Puducherry, the byelection for which was won by the BJP's ally, the All India NR Congress."Recently, byelections were held in Assam, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. I want to inform the people of the country today that the Congress party did not win a single seat. In Nagaon, the BJP candidate won by a margin of 1,42,000 votes, wresting the seat from the Congress. In Nandigram, the BJP candidate won with 76% of the vote, securing a massive lead of 1,22,000 votes. In Rejinagar, the BJP won by over 75,000 votes, snatching the seat from the Trinamool, while in Puducherry, the NDA candidate from ally AINRC won by 8,482 votes. The Congress secured only 22% of the votes," Shah said.His remarks came shortly after leaders of the Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc held a joint press conference at Rahul Gandhi's residence in New Delhi, where they vowed to continue their campaign for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the invalidation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls over alleged irregularities in the exercise.The Indian Express reported last month that the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had raised objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they claimed were taken without their knowledge, including those related to the SIR.The report brought further scrutiny on Kumar, who has repeatedly been accused by the opposition of facilitating “vote chori” (vote theft) in favour of the BJP since becoming CEC in 2025.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Ex-Met Police officer on trial accused of rape
articles.summary: Mark Tyrrell raped and sexually assaulted a woman over about two years, his trial is told.
articles.body:
A former Metropolitan Police officer accused of raping a woman was specially trained to deal with victims of sexual offences, a court has heard.

Mark Tyrrell, 57, denies two counts of rape, 11 of sexual assault and four of assault by penetration against the woman over about two years while he was serving with the force.

Opening his trial at Southwark Crown Court, prosecutor Catherine Farrelly KC said Tyrrell had been trained in Sexual Offences Investigation Techniques.

Jurors heard concerns were first raised when officers visited the woman's home on an unrelated matter and found Tyrrell hiding beside her bed.

He later phoned her and said nothing sexual had happened, the court was told.

Tyrrell is also accused of perverting the course of justice by trying to delete messages between them. In one, he apologised for "being a sex offender" and for ruining her life, jurors heard. When she told him not to say such things, he replied that they were true.

The prosecution alleges Tyrrell raped the woman by having sex with her after she had repeatedly said no.

Afterwards, he allegedly asked whether she realised that what he had done "was rape", and said he would report himself and would undoubtedly go to prison, Farrelly said.

The woman alleges that on several occasions she woke to find Tyrrell penetrating her, despite having refused sex the night before.

On one occasion, when she asked him what had happened, he shouted at her and asked whether she realised what she was saying and what could happen to him, the prosecutor told the court.

Jurors heard the woman kept a list of incidents involving Tyrrell, including the alleged sexual assaults.

In a police interview, she said she had felt pressured by him and feared no-one would believe her because she could not prove what had happened. She was also worried police would protect him because he was an officer, the court heard.

After his arrest, Tyrrell denied ever having sex with her.

Tyrrell, of Meltham, West Yorkshire, has admitted misconduct in public office. He has also pleaded guilty to a separate count of perverting the course of justice by persuading the woman to lie to police about why he was in her bedroom.

articles.title: 42-year-old man dies after falling off Six Flags roller coaster: Police
articles.summary: The incident occurred Monday at Six Flags Over Georgia in Cobb County.
articles.body:
A 42-year-old man died after being ejected from a roller coaster at a Six Flags amusement park in Georgia, police said.

The man -- Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, of Atlanta -- was found dead beneath the ride at Six Flags Over Georgia on Monday, according to the Cobb County Police Department.

"Preliminary information gathered through witness and employee interviews indicates Kariem was ejected from the ride and struck other patrons before falling beneath the attraction," the Cobb County Police Department said in a statement on Tuesday. "Investigators continue to examine the circumstances surrounding the incident."

The state's Office of the Commissioner of Insurance and Safety Fire, which is responsible for the safety of amusement park rides in Georgia, also said it is "actively investigating" the incident.

"Our investigative team is conducting an in‑depth and comprehensive review to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident and to ensure full compliance with all applicable policies and procedures," Garrison Bennett, the agency's press secretary, said in a statement on Tuesday.

Several people were also injured in the incident, which occurred shortly before 4 p.m. Monday at the Atlanta-area amusement park, according to police.

Distraught witnesses described the horrific incident to a local station , saying they saw a man fall from the amusement park's Goliath roller coaster and hit the ride several times, and that the fall was captured on their souvenir pictures.

Riders on the Goliath were seen being evacuated off the roller coaster on Monday, after it stopped near the top of the ride.

A Six Flags spokesperson said that the "park team and local authorities responded immediately, and we are cooperating fully with local authorities as they complete their investigation."

"We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today," the spokesperson said in a statement. "Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the guest's family, friends, and loved ones. We are also providing support to the guests and team members affected."

The spokesperson said that "out of an abundance of caution," Six Flags has "temporarily closed similar attractions across our parks."

Six Flags is not releasing additional information on the incident at this time "out of respect for the family's privacy," the spokesperson added.

The Goliath roller coaster reaches an elevation of 200 feet and speeds up to 70 mph, according to the amusement park's website. The ride first opened in 2006 at the amusement park, located west of Atlanta in Austell.

The manufacturer of the Goliath coaster, Switzerland-based Bolliger & Mabillard, said the company is "deeply saddened by this tragic accident."

"Our thoughts are with the family and those affected," Olivier Bolliger of Bolliger & Mabillard said in a statement Tuesday. "We are actively investigating the incident and will not comment further until we have a better understanding of what happened."

articles.title: Hyundai Motor Group to invest $15.5 bn in India till 2032
articles.summary: Hyundai Motor Group to invest $15.5bn in India from 2026-2032 to expand manufacturing, R&D, local sourcing and EV mobility, boosting exports and jobs.
articles.body: Chennai: Hyundai Motor Group will invest $15.5 billion in India between 2026 and 2032 to expand manufacturing, research and development, local sourcing and future mobility technologies, positioning the country as a key production and export hub.The investment was announced following a meeting between Hyundai Motor Group executive chair Euisun Chung and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Tuesday.The seven-year investment will cover manufacturing expansion at Hyundai Motor India and Kia India, R&D infrastructure, supplier development and emerging mobility businesses. The group will also establish a dedicated investment entity in India to coordinate capital deployment and strategic partnerships.The group plans to invest about $700 million in its Indian R&D centre, including a vehicle testing track, to accelerate the development of next-generation automotive technologies.The investment will also support local suppliers, emerging mobility startups and new business areas such as EV charging infrastructure, vehicle recycling and automotive financing. It is also expected to generate employment across manufacturing, engineering, R&D and supply chains while strengthening India’s role in the group’s global operations and exports.“India remains one of Hyundai Motor Group’s most important and strategic markets globally. The past 30 years have been defined by our commitment to India. This investment reaffirms our commitment to India for the next 30 years and beyond,” Chung said, adding that it would create employment opportunities and support industrial development.Hyundai Motor Group has an annual vehicle manufacturing capacity of more than 1.4 million units in India across Hyundai Motor India’s facilities in Chennai (824,000 units) and Pune (170,000 units), and Kia India’s plant in Anantapur (431,000 units). The group employs more than 24,000 people in the country.At its 2026 CEO Investor Day, held in Seoul in August, the South Korean automaker unveiled plans to launch or update 26 models in India by 2030. These will include new products, full model changes, enhancements and new powertrain options as part of its global growth strategy.
